source: ESPN NBA league injury designations plus NBA game lineup state

freshnessPolicy.missingReportMeaning: No injury report was matched; this is not a confirmed healthy designation.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Carter (illness) practiced with the G League's Maine Celtics on Wednesday.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Carter is working back from mononucleosis, which has prevented him from making his season debut. A two-way player, Carter figures to begin his season in Maine as opposed to Boston once healthy.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Head coach Charles Lee said Miller (groin) will be re-evaluated over the weekend, and they expect to have more information by Monday, Steve Reed of The Associated Press reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Lee downplayed the groin issue after the game, saying he didn't see exactly when the injury occurred but noticed Miller started limping, and he asked for a sub after a couple of plays. He was ruled out after heading back to the locker room, and Tidjane Salaun started the second half for him. If Miller needs to miss additional time, Coby White and Naz Reid would be asked to step it up on offense, and there would be more minutes available for Salaun and Sion James.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Schroder (thigh) is out for Friday's game versus Boston.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Schroder is sitting out Friday for the first time this season due to left thigh soreness. With the veteran floor general sidelined, Coby White should see his minutes climb into the 20s for the first time this year as he works back from a preseason calf strain.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Diabate (quadriceps) has been ruled out for Friday's game against Boston, according to the Hornets' official injury report.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Diabate's absence will leave Charlotte shorthanded in the frontcourt against the Celtics. Ryan Kalkbrenner could see additional opportunities at center, while other available big men may also absorb minutes. Diabate's next opportunity to play will come Monday against Cleveland.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Knueppel (hamstring) is out for Friday's game against the Celtics.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Knueppel re-aggravated his left hamstring strain in his season debut Wednesday against Brooklyn. The Hornets haven't yet indicated the sharpshooter is facing a multi-week absence, but they'll likely proceed with caution. Grayson Allen is back in the mix as a high-end fantasy streaming option for as long as Knueppel is out.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: The Hornets recalled Williams (hamstring) from the G League's Greensboro Swarm on Wednesday.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Williams has yet to make his season debut due to a right hamstring strain. However, he appears to be making progress after joining the Swarm for practice Wednesday.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Collins didn't practice Friday due to an illness, per K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Collins left Wednesday's loss to the Knicks early, presumably due to the ailment. For now, he can be tentatively labeled as questionable for Saturday's game versus the 76ers.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Head coach Tiago Splittler said Friday that Claxton (hamstring) is expected to make his season debut Sunday against the 76ers, per Joel Lorenzi of The Athletic.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Splitter stopped short of confirming Claxton's availability, but the big man is certainly trending in the right direction. Once Claxton is cleared to make his Bulls debut, Jalen Smith (hand) is likely to fall into a reserve role.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Smith (hand) won't return to Wednesday's game against the Knicks.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Smith has been starting for Nic Claxton (hamstring), who hasn't played this season. However, the Bulls will be down another big, at least for the remainder of Wednesday's contest. As a result, Zach Collins should handle most of the minutes in the middle the rest of the way.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: De Larrea (knee) is out for Friday's game against Utah.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: De Larrea continues to miss time with a right knee strain, and it's not clear at this time where he's at in his rehab. He can be considered week-to-week until further notice.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Biberovic (heel) is listed as out for Monday's game against Sacramento.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Biberovic has been battling inflammation in his right heel, preventing him from making his NBA debut. While the rookie should be considered week-to-week, he likely has a way to go before earning a meaningful role in Dallas even when he's cleared to suit up.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Lively (foot) is listed as out for Monday's game against the Kings.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Although there haven't been any negative reports regarding Lively's rehab progress, it doesn't appear he will be back in the lineup anytime soon. For now, the 22-year-old should be considered week-to-week. While Lively remains on the shelf, Daniel Gafford and Moussa Cisse should continue to handle most of the work at the five. Santi Aldama (knee) might also get involved in that area once he's cleared to return.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Joe (hip) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against Philadelphia.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Joe will miss Wednesday's contest due to a right hip contusion, resulting in his fifth straight absence. This will continue to open up additional minutes on the perimeter for Detroit's reserves. Joe's next opportunity to play will come Sunday against the Lakers.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Duren will be re-evaluated in two weeks due to a right hamstring strain, Eric Vincent of ClutchPoints.com reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Duren suffered the hamstring injury in Friday's win over Miami and is set to miss an extended period. Paul Reed is expected to join the starting five and carries significant fantasy value until Duren returns. John Collins and Tolu Smith are also candidates to see a bump in minutes in Duren's stead.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Ingram (Achilles) has progressed to full contact basketball activities, per NBA writer Justin Russo.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Ingram told reporters Friday he's close to returning, though a concrete timeline for his season debut has yet to be disclosed. The star forward is recovery from a partial Achilles tear, and it sounds like he'll be ready to roll at some point in mid-November.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: The Clippers recalled Niederhauser (foot) from the G League's San Diego Clippers on Sunday.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Niederhauser remains unlikely to play a meaningful role in the short term following a seven-month recovery from foot surgery. The 23-year-old might instead make a phased return to action, possibly seeing limited minutes at some point in upcoming weeks and making some appearances in the G League. Last season, he averaged 4.3 points, 2.9 rebounds and 0.3 assists per regular-season game during his rookie year.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Beal (knee) will not be ready for the start of the regular season, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Beal is dealing with knee inflammation that will keep him sidelined for Opening Night. While it's unclear how long the Clippers will be without the veteran guard, Darius Garland, Keaton Wagler and Kris Dunn should dominate the backcourt minutes in his absence. Beal's 2025-26 campaign was cut short by a hip injury after he averaged 8.2 points and 1.7 assists in 20.6 minutes across just six regular-season appearances.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Miller underwent surgery Wednesday to repair a torn left rotator cuff and will be re-evaluated in six months, per Law Murray of The Athletic.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: It's a tough break for Miller, who had an opportunity to battle for a reserve role during training camp in the fall. The timeline for a return is likely to keep him on the shelf until after the All-Star break. Miller's extended stay on the sidelines gives Kobe Sanders a chance to crack the Clippers' rotation.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Stewart (knee) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Thunder.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Stewart suffered a right knee bone bruise in Wednesday's loss to the Pacers and will hit the inactive list Thursday. His next opportunity to play will come Monday at Toronto. Quinten Post figures to see increased burn for as long as Stewart is sidelined.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Pippen (back) has been ruled out for Friday's game against Oklahoma City.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Pippen is set for his fourth consecutive absence while dealing with a back issue. His next opportunity to return will arrive Monday in Toronto.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Jones (ankle/two-way player) is out for Friday's game against Toronto.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: It's not clear whether Jones is still dealing with a right ankle injury, or if he's been ruled out due to his status as a two-way player. He'll presumably open the year with the G League's Wisconsin Herd once he's back at full strength.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Beringer was ruled out for the second half of Friday's game against the Pelicans due to a nasal fracture, Dane Moore of 'The Dane Moore NBA Podcast' reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Although Beringer's nasal fracture will prevent him from returning to Friday's contest, he may be able to play through the injury during future games while wearing a mask. Trey Lyles stands to benefit from increased minutes in the meantime.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Shannon (hip) has been ruled out for Friday's game against New Orleans.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Shannon's absence will leave Minnesota a bit shorthanded on the wing. His limited role makes the absence unlikely to have a significant fantasy impact, though the Timberwolves could distribute his available minutes among their remaining perimeter players.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Edwards underwent a successful arthroscopic procedure on his right knee Thursday, the Timberwolves announced.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Edwards underwent debridement surgery in Minnesota, though the team did not provide a timetable for his return. The star guard is expected to make a full recovery, with additional updates coming as he progresses through rehabilitation. Based on previous reporting from ESPN's Shams Charania, Edwards could miss up to two months. Edwards was off to a scorching start this season, averaging 33.3 points, 4.8 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 2.0 steals across four appearances.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: DiVincenzo (Achilles) remains confident that he'll return during the 2026-27 season, Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: DiVincenzo is approaching six months since tearing his right Achilles during the first round of the playoffs and has been rehabbing with the expectation that he'll play at some point this season. The veteran guard has sought advice from Jayson Tatum, Tyrese Haliburton and Damian Lillard during his recovery, though Minnesota has yet to establish a timetable for his return.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Missi (knee) is out for Friday's game against Minnesota.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Missi has been sidelined since picking up his injury Oct. 23. He remains without a timetable to return.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Bona (neck) is listed as out for Friday's game versus the Cavaliers.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: While Bona isn't starting Friday, his absence will open up minutes behind Joel Embiid. With Dominick Barlow (back) also sidelined against Cleveland, the 76ers should need more minutes out of Jabari Walker. Tacko Fall might also see action for the first time of the 2026-27 season.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Head coach Nick Nurse said Wednesday that Barlow (back) likely needs another 10-12 days before he's cleared to return to the court, Derek Bodner of AllPHLY.com reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Nurse added that the team is "pretty positive" that Barlow's back is getting better, though he's still going to have to wait some more time before being cleared. The big man has yet to make his season debut due to a lumbar spine bone stress response, and he isn't expected to return until mid-November at the earliest.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Hukporti has sustained a season-ending ruptured right Achilles tendon, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Hukporti went down with an Achilles injury in Monday's preseason opener against the Knicks, and an MRI has since revealed a rupture. He signed a one-year deal with the 76ers over the summer, so Hukporti will be an unrestricted free agent come season's end. With Hukporti's year already finished, Adem Bona (foot) should assume the backup center role behind Joel Embiid once healthy.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Hunter (illness) is listed as out for Friday's game against San Antonio.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Hunter was listed as questionable but has now been ruled out for the first time this season. His next opportunity to play will come Sunday versus the Heat. Without Hunter, Malik Monk might find his way into the starting lineup.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Raynaud (knee) is progressing in his rehabilitation and will be re-evaluated in approximately two weeks, Brenden Nunes of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140 reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Raynaud's absence is expected to extend into mid-November due to a right patellar subluxation. With Dylan Cardwell (calf) set to miss at least one more week, Precious Achiuwa, Jonathan Mogbo and De'Andre Hunter are candidates for increased minutes in the frontcourt.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Murray (ankle) will be re-evaluated in 10-to-14 days, NBA reporter Marc Stein reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Murray has officially been diagnosed with left ankle capsulitis, and he's set to miss at least the next 10 days. Precious Achiuwa has been starting in Murray's absence, and he should continue to see opportunities along with De'Andre Hunter and Daeqwon Plowden.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Simmons underwent successful surgery Tuesday to repair a torn right Achilles tendon, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Simmons had a quality preseason, averaging 10.5 points, 4.0 rebounds and 4.0 assists over 17.4 minutes per contest (two games). The 30-year-old was on track to suit up for the Kings on opening night, though those plans were halted after he suffered a torn Achilles tendon during practice. Now, Simmons will focus on rehab. However, it's unknown what the future holds regarding his career in the NBA.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Barnes (adductor) is listed as out for Friday's game against Milwaukee, Michael Grange of Sportsnet.ca reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Barnes will miss his first game of the 2026-27 campaign Friday, and his next chance to suit up will come Monday in Memphis. With Immanuel Quickley (hamstring) and Kawhi Leonard (knee) sidelined as well, RJ Barrett, Ja'Kobe Walter, Jamal Shead and Collin Murray-Boyles are expected to be the Raptors' top offensive contributors, regardless of who starts.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Quickley (hamstring) won't play Friday in Milwaukee, Michael Grange of Sportsnet.ca reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: This will be Quickley's first missed game of the season, and for now, he should be considered questionable for Monday's meeting with Memphis. Jamal Shead will likely start in his absence and Malachi Smith will have a chance to get into the rotation.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Leonard has completed treatment to reduce swelling in his left knee and he will be re-evaluated in one week, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Leonard will now begin the next phase of his rehab, and while he'll be re-evaluated by Nov. 10, it's still unlikely we'll see him back on the floor until the end of November. Ja'Kobe Walter should continue to start while Leonard is sidelined, and it'll be Scottie Barnes, Immanuel Quickley and RJ Barrett running the show on offense.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Bittle (foot) is out for Monday's game against the Clippers and remains without a timetable to return.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: For now, fantasy managers can assume that he's week-to-week. He's not expected to crack the rotation upon his return.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Nurkic (toe) has begun participating in on-court activities as he continues recovering from a right foot injury sustained during an Oct. 4 preseason game against Denver. He will be re-evaluated in two weeks, the Jazz announced Friday.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Nurkic is progressing in his recovery, but the two-week re-evaluation timeline indicates he remains some distance from returning to game action. His absence should continue to create opportunities in Utah's frontcourt, with Jaxson Hayes and Mo Bamba among the players positioned to benefit from additional playing time. Nurkic's next evaluation will provide a clearer picture of his potential return date.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Jackson has been diagnosed with a torn MCL in his right knee and will be sidelined for 6-to-8 weeks, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Jackson sustained the injury early in Monday's loss to Memphis, and he's now expected to miss at least a month and a half of action. The star big man's absence creates a major void in the Utah lineup, one that is likely to be filled by a timeshare of Jaxson Hayes (shoulder), Kyle Filipowski and Mo Bamba. The Jazz could also shift Lauri Markkanen (wrist), when healthy, to the center spot at times, perhaps allowing Ace Bailey to spend more time at power forward.

unmatchedInjuries.shortComment: Alexander won't play Wednesday against the Grizzlies due to a left knee bone bruise.
unmatchedInjuries.detail: Alexander sat out Friday's preseason finale with what the team initially described as a left knee injury, but we now know he's dealing with a bone bruise. Don't be surprised if Alexander misses Friday's game against the Pelicans as well.

injury.shortComment: Furphy (knee) is practicing with the G League's Noblesville Boom, per Alex Golden of SI.com.
injury.detail: The Pacers have been pretty quiet regarding Furphy's ACL recovery since the offseason, but it's encouraging to hear some form of progress as the forward begins to ramp up his activity. Although Furphy still lacks a firm timetable for a return and is likely to be brought back slowly, it appears a season debut before the start of the new calendar year is in the cards.

injury.shortComment: Haliburton (hamstring) will miss at least the next two weeks of action, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
injury.detail: Given the tricky nature of hamstring injuries, the Pacers will likely take their time bringing Haliburton back to the court, so don't be surprised if his absence extends beyond this two-week window. Andrew Nembhard (neck) and Pascal Siakam should each get a usage bump as they take over more of the playmaking duties sans Haliburton and there will be more minutes available for Quenton Jackson.

injury.shortComment: McConnell (hamstring) is questionable for Saturday's game against Denver.
injury.detail: McConnell has a chance to make his season debut Saturday. The veteran floor general is likely to have a minutes restriction if he's cleared to play, though less playing time would be available to Quenton Jackson.

injury.shortComment: Oubre (calf) is questionable for Saturday's game against Denver.
injury.detail: Oubre is trying to end a two-game absence Saturday due to a calf contusion. Less playing time would be open to Jarace Walker and Obi Toppin if Oubre is able to return.

injury.shortComment: Head coach Rick Carlise confirmed Sheppard will miss "months" after undergoing surgery to repair a torn meniscus in his left knee, Tony East of Forbes.com reports.
injury.detail: Sheppard required a full repair and is without a definitive timetable for a return to action. With Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) expected to miss at least two weeks, Quenton Jackson figures to see a significant uptick in playing time. Two-way player Braden Smith could also see increased action with the parent club.

injury.shortComment: DeRozan (back) is probable for Saturday's game against the Pacers.
injury.detail: The veteran forward is expected to end a one-game absence Saturday due to lower-back spasms. It's been a sluggish start to DeRozan's Nuggets tenure -- he's reached the 15-point marker just one time over his first six appearances in 2026-27.

injury.shortComment: Strawther (knee) was diagnosed with a left knee sprain Friday and will be re-evaluated in six weeks, Vinny Benedetto of The Denver Gazette reports.
injury.detail: Strawther suffered the injury in Wednesday's preseason game against the Clippers. The 24-year-old has appeared in 172 regular-season games for the Nuggets since entering the league in 2023, averaging 7.1 points, 2.0 rebounds and 1.1 assists over 16.2 minutes per contest. He was in line to compete for an expanded role during the 2026-27 campaign. While that may be the case once Strawther is cleared to suit up, Tyus Jones and potentially Ryan Nembhard are candidates to receive more minutes in the interim.

injury.shortComment: Gilbert is out for Friday's game against the Wizards due to left knee inflammation.
injury.detail: Gilbert, who is on a two-way deal with Atlanta, will presumably begin the season with the G League's College Park Skyhawks once he returns to health. He can be considered day-to-day until more information on his injury comes to light.

injury.shortComment: Gueye underwent surgery Tuesday to repair a fractured left foot that he suffered during a workout last week, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
injury.detail: Gueye will be re-evaluated by medical staff in 3-to-4 months, which means he'll miss all of training camp and preseason and likely the start of the 2026-27 regular season. It's a brutal blow for the fourth-year big man, given that the Hawks used the No. 23 overall pick of the 2026 NBA Draft to select St. John's product Zuby Ejiofor. Gueye's absence means Ejiofor will have more opportunities in the preseason, and the rookie could establish a key role off the bench behind Onyeka Okongwu and projected backup center Jock Landale (ankle).

injury.shortComment: Johnson (ankle) is out for Friday's game against the Wizards.
injury.detail: This will be Johnson's third straight game on the sidelines, and for now, he should be considered questionable for Saturday's meeting with the Nets. Luguentz Dort should continue to start in his absence, while Nickeil Alexander-Walker and Onyeka Okongwu will see a larger role on offense.

injury.shortComment: Landale (hip) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Wizards.
injury.detail: A left hip strain will force Landale to miss a third straight game on Friday. Onyeka Okongwu and rookie first-round pick Zuby Ejiofor will continue to hold down the frontcourt with Landale sidelined. His next chance to suit up will come against the Nets on Saturday in the second half of Atlanta's back-to-back.

injury.shortComment: Newell (toe) is out for Friday's game against Washington.
injury.detail: Newell suffered a left big toe injury Wednesday against Washington and was unable to return. The injury will force him to miss at least one additional game. Newell can be considered day-to-day going forward.

injury.shortComment: Veesaar was diagnosed with a torn right ACL and is expected to miss the 2026-27 season, the Hawks announced Monday.
injury.detail: Veesaar suffered the injury during a workout on Sept. 15, and an MRI confirmed the diagnosis. The No. 52 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, Veesaar was expected to spend a lot of time with Atlanta's G League affiliate this season.

injury.shortComment: Bilodeau (shoulder) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Indiana.
injury.detail: Bilodeau will miss a third straight game to begin the regular season due to a right shoulder sprain. The two-way player's absence shouldn't affect the rotation.

injury.shortComment: The Nets exercised Demin's third-year team option for the 2027-28 season, Sharif Phillips-Keaton of USA Today reports Thursday.
injury.detail: Brooklyn's decision keeps Demin under contract through the 2027-28 campaign as the organization continues investing in its young backcourt. The move provides additional long-term stability but doesn't directly impact his immediate fantasy outlook. Demin is currently dealing with a right leg bone bruise and is scheduled to be re-evaluated in one week.

injury.shortComment: Sharpe registered 15 points (5-7 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 4-5 FT), 13 rebounds and four assists across 26 minutes in Sunday's 98-90 win over the Pacers.
injury.detail: Sharpe dominated the glass, collecting four offensive rebounds while shooting efficiently en route to his first double-double of the season. It was also the second time he scored in double digits this season. Sharpe's rebounding provides a useful foundation, although his ceiling will depend on whether Brooklyn consistently gives him enough touches and playing time -- he has played more than 25 minutes just twice all season long.

injury.shortComment: Allen (knee) is out for Friday's game against the 76ers.
injury.detail: Allen will sit out the first leg of this back-to-back set after tweaking his knee in Wednesday's 124-116 loss to the Thunder, and for now, he should be considered questionable for Saturday's matchup with the Knicks. Evan Mobley will spend more time at center with Allen unavailable and Thomas Bryant could see a bump in minutes.

injury.shortComment: Merrill (elbow) won't return to Friday's game against the 76ers, Dave McMenamin of ESPN.com reports.
injury.detail: Merrill has been dealing with a right elbow issue since the preseason. While he hasn't missed any games during the regular season, he's now in danger of missing Saturday's game against the Knicks. If Merrill can't play in that contest, Meleek Thomas and Tyrese Proctor could see more playing time.

injury.shortComment: Tyson (ankle) is out for Friday's game against the 76ers.
injury.detail: Tyson continues to recover from a sprained ankle. Until he's cleared to retake the floor, Mario Hezonja and Meleek Thomas should continue to play meaningful roles off the bench for the Cavaliers.

injury.shortComment: Hart is out for Saturday's game against the Cavaliers due to right ankle soreness.
injury.detail: Hart practiced Friday, per Steve Popper of Newsday, but he's getting a bit more time to recover. Landry Shamet should draw a second consecutive start for the Knicks on Saturday.

injury.shortComment: Holmgren underwent a biological treatment Friday to address a small patellar tendon tear and will miss at least 8-10 weeks, Nick Crain of Slam reports.
injury.detail: This is another massive blow to an Oklahoma City squad that's already set to be without Jalen Williams (leg) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) for most, if not all, of the season. With Holmgren sidelined, Kenrich Williams, Jaylin Williams and Aday Mara are all candidates to see increased playing time. Two-way player Brooks Barnhizer could also see more minutes.

injury.shortComment: Sorber (knee) is out for Wednesday's game against the Cavaliers.
injury.detail: Sorber remains in recovery mode due to knee surgery. Until the Thunder update his timetable for a return, Sorber can be deemed week-to-week.

injury.shortComment: Topic (back) is listed as out for Wednesday's game against Cleveland.
injury.detail: Topic has yet to play during the 2026-27 campaign, and at this rate, it doesn't look like he will be on the floor anytime soon. For now, he should be considered week-to-week. The 2024 No. 12 overall pick has appeared in only 10 regular-season games throughout his career, averaging 5.2 points, 1.9 rebounds and 4.4 assists while shooting 40.0 percent from deep over 16.0 minutes per contest.

injury.shortComment: Wallace underwent surgery Friday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Clemente Almanza of USA Today reports.
injury.detail: Wallace is expected to miss most, if not all, of the season. However, there's still a chance he will return late in the campaign after sustaining the shoulder injury in Sunday's win over the Clippers. With Jalen Williams (leg) also set to be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Alex Caruso (ankle) should see significant playing time once cleared to return. In the meantime, Jared McCain, Bennett Stirtz and Josh Dix are expected to see increased burn.

injury.shortComment: Williams (leg) underwent successful surgery Wednesday to "address a fractured left fibula and reconstruction of ankle ligaments following a fracture and dislocation." He will be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Tim MacMahon of ESPN.com reports.
injury.detail: Williams suffered the injury during Sunday's meeting with the Clippers and was taken off the court on a stretcher. It's unknown when the 25-year-old will be cleared to return, though the Thunder will presumably be overly cautious moving forward. Williams, who signed a five-year extension in July of 2025, has had a productive career, averaging 17.9 points, 4.6 rebounds, 4.4 assists and 1.3 steals over 30.9 minutes per contest. However, after playing at least 69 regular-season games in his first three years in the league, he has appeared in just 36 in the last two seasons combined. With the Thunder having one of the deepest rosters in the NBA, the team may look for more minutes from Jared McCain, Jaylin Williams, and Kenrich Williams for the remainder of the 2026-27 campaign.

injury.shortComment: Williams (back) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Grizzlies.
injury.detail: Williams missed Wednesday's 124-116 victory over Cleveland with lower back spasms, and he'll now miss two straight games with the ailment. Micah Peavy, Kenrich Williams and Aday Mara will continue to play significant roles for the injury-riddled Thunder.

injury.shortComment: The Wizards announced Monday that Beekman sustained a right acromioclavicular joint injury and will be re-evaluated in approximately three weeks.
injury.detail: Beekman is set for an extended absence, with his re-evaluation timeline suggesting he could remain sidelined beyond the initial three-week window. The injury further limits Washington's backcourt depth, though Beekman's absence is unlikely to have a significant impact on standard fantasy leagues.

injury.shortComment: Champagnie (foot) is expected to miss several months, per Josh Robbins of The Athletic.
injury.detail: The forward underwent surgery Wednesday to address a fractured foot, and the Wizards hope Champagnie will be ready to return at some time around the All-Star break in February. The likes of Bilal Coulibaly, Tre Johnson and Bub Carrington will all be asked to help pick up the slack for the foreseeable future.

injury.shortComment: Davis (ankle) is listed as out for Friday's game against the Hawks.
injury.detail: Atlanta is shorthanded, but Washington will also be without one of its top players, with Davis missing his first game of the 2026-27 campaign due to an ankle injury that he picked up when these clubs met Wednesday. As a result, the Wizards may look to Will Riley and Khris Middleton to fill most of the void at the four spot.

injury.shortComment: Vukcevic (hip) is listed as out for Monday's game against Orlando.
injury.detail: The Wizards announced on Oct. 1 that Vukcevic would be sidelined for at least a month. However, there haven't been any definitive updates regarding when he will be able to get back on the floor. In the meantime, Deandre Ayton should see more minutes off the bench.

injury.shortComment: The Wizards announced Thursday that Watkins has undergone surgery for a torn ACL.
injury.detail: Watkins, a two-way player for the Wizards, suffered the injury during the Summer League. Although Washington has yet to offer a timetable for a return, a typical recovery time for the procedure is approximately 9-to-12 months. That leaves Watkins in serious jeopardy of missing most, if not all, of the 2026-27 season, and it remains to be seen if the team will continue keeping him around on a two-way roster spot while he's injured.

injury.shortComment: Butler (knee) could return sometime between January and February as he continues recovering from a torn right ACL, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports.
injury.detail: Butler, who underwent surgery after suffering the injury Jan. 19, has progressed to individual court work but still has several rehabilitation milestones to clear. His next step involves landing comfortably after a game-speed jump. Coach Steve Kerr is hopeful Butler can rejoin Golden State for the latter portion of the season, though no official return date has been announced. The 37-year-old forward remains a significant part of the Warriors' plans and could provide a substantial boost during the second half of the campaign.

injury.shortComment: Green (elbow) is listed as questionable ahead of Saturday's game against Orlando.
injury.detail: Green is coming off an 11-assist performance in Thursday's 120-100 win over the Heat. He's in danger of missing his third contest of the 2026-27 campaign due to elbow inflammation. If Green is downgraded to out, Charles Bassey and Al Horford would likely split time at the five.

injury.shortComment: Moody (knee) is progressing toward a potential return between December and January after rupturing his left patellar tendon in March, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports.
injury.detail: Moody has been limited to individual court work, but team sources indicate he's ahead of Jimmy Butler (knee) in the rehabilitation process and is expected to return before the veteran forward. The 24-year-old still has several recovery checkpoints to complete, and Golden State has not established an official timetable. His eventual return would help replenish a Warriors wing rotation that will open the season without both Moody and Butler.

injury.shortComment: Payton is questionable to play Saturday against the Magic due to right calf tightness.
injury.detail: We'll have a better idea on Payton's status based on his activity level at Saturday's shootaround, but if he's forced to the sidelines, that would open up some minutes for Brandon Williams and De'Anthony Melton. LJ Cryer would also have the opportunity to get into the rotation sans Payton.

injury.shortComment: Porzingis announced on his social media that he's stepping away from basketball.
injury.detail: Porzingis said he was looking forward to joining the Warriors, but his body didn't respond the way he wanted it too during his ramp-up process before the season. Additionally, he said he will work with the Warriors on a solution that "makes sense." Porzingis is making this decision to prioritize his health and will hopefully turn a corner soon on that front.

injury.shortComment: Santos (knee) is questionable for Saturday's game versus Orlando, per Nick Friedell of The Athletic.
injury.detail: Santos is feeling better, having participated in Friday's practice. Will Richard would likely retreat back to the bench if Santos is able to suit up Saturday.

injury.shortComment: Banchero is expected to be sidelined for the next four-to-six weeks due to a right high-ankle sprain, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
injury.detail: Banchero left during Friday's loss against the Timberwolves due to an ankle injury, and follow-up tests have confirmed a high-ankle sprain for the fifth-year forward. With an extended absence expected, the Magic will have to rely more heavily on Franz Wagner and Desmond Bane offensively, and Tristan da Silva figures to be the top candidate to enter the Magic's starting lineup for as long as Banchero is sidelined.

injury.shortComment: Orlando recalled Isaac (knee) from the G League's Osceola Magic on Wednesday.
injury.detail: Isaac was assigned to Osceola but recalled again on the same day while he continued his recovery from a knee issue. Having yet to play this season, the forward is not expected to find a meaningful role in the short term, and he'll likely appear on the bench when he's available again.

injury.shortComment: Team president Jeff Weltman said Monday that Nelson (ankle) remains about a month away from returning to the court after offseason surgery, per Philip Rossman-Reich of OrlandoMagicDaily.com.
injury.detail: With Nelson still in recovery mode from the left ankle surgery he underwent this summer, his path back to game action remains delayed for the early part of the season. The rookie big man is on a two-way contract with the Magic, so his short-term absence mainly affects his developmental timeline rather than Orlando's regular rotation.

injury.shortComment: Penda was diagnosed with a partially torn right hamstring Saturday, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
injury.detail: Penda suffered the hamstring tear in Friday's 136-115 preseason win over the Heat. It's unknown how long the injury will keep the 21-year-old off the floor. However, since it's a different injury than the one he suffered in the same hamstring during training camp, the team may take a cautious approach regarding his return. Penda, the No. 32 overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft, averaged 3.8 points, 3.2 rebounds and 1.2 assists over 12.8 minutes per outing in 59 regular-season games in 2025-26. While he's not expected to be a mainstay in the rotation throughout the 2026-27 campaign, his absence could open up a few minutes for Tristan Da Silva.

injury.shortComment: Suggs has been diagnosed with a mild bone bruise in his right knee and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
injury.detail: Suggs suffered the injury during Sunday's win over the Knicks when his right knee buckled following a layup attempt. Fortunately, further testing revealed no major structural damage, though the 25-year-old will miss at least two weeks before being re-evaluated. Anthony Black and Jase Richardson could see increased opportunities in Orlando's backcourt during Suggs' absence.

injury.shortComment: Fleming (ankle) is questionable for Saturday's game against the Rockets.
injury.detail: Fleming missed the Suns' last game and could be in line to miss a second straight contest due to a sprained left ankle. His absence shouldn't carry a ton of fantasy appeal, as he's averaging just 0.5 points and 1.5 rebounds in two outings off the bench this season.

injury.shortComment: Goodwin (calf) is doubtful for Saturday's game against the Rockets.
injury.detail: Goodwin is on track to miss his third straight game, which should lead to more minutes for Luke Kennard. Check back for official confirmation on Goodwin's status closer to Saturday's tipoff.

injury.shortComment: Williams underwent surgery Thursday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will miss an extended period of time, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
injury.detail: This is a tough blow for the center with training camp right around the corner. With his status for Opening Night in jeopardy, this will put a lot of eyes on Oso Ighodaro and Khaman Maluach, with the latter already drawing buzz during the Summer League. More clarity on Williams' timeline should be known in the coming weeks.

injury.shortComment: Head coach Ime Udoka said Wednesday that Adams (calf) is still without a timetable to return and will be evaluated on a "weekly basis," Varun Shankar of the Houston Chronicle reports.
injury.detail: Adams hasn't played since Oct. 23 due to a right soleus strain and remains without a definitive timetable to return. Oscar Tshiebwe figures to see increased burn until Capela (ankle) or Adams returns.

injury.shortComment: Capela (ankle) is out for Saturday's game against the Suns.
injury.detail: The veteran big man is managing a sprained right ankle, which is costing him a third consecutive contest. His next chance to return arrives Monday, when the Rockets host the Nuggets.

injury.shortComment: Head coach Micah Nori said that Krejci suffered a left leg fracture during Wednesday's 132-119 win over the Suns, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
injury.detail: Nori did not provide a timetable for Krejci, but it's safe to say that he won't be back soon. His minutes figure to be divvied up amongst Chris Youngblood and Sidy Cissoko.

injury.shortComment: Morant has been diagnosed with a Grade 2 left hamstring strain and is expected to miss four weeks, Portland announced Friday.
injury.detail: Morant left Thursday's game early with a hamstring injury, which has since been revealed to be a strain that will result in a monthlong absence. The star guard leaves a major void in the Trail Blazers' starting backcourt, one that figures to be filled by Jrue Holiday for the foreseeable future.

injury.shortComment: Sharpe suffered a torn meniscus in his knee and is expected to miss six months, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
injury.detail: It's a tough blow to the Trail Blazers' depth on the wing ahead of training camp. Sharpe, who is now likely to be sidelined until after the All-Star break, had been ticketed for a reserve role behind Toumani Camara following an injury-plagued 2025-26 campaign, which saw average a career-high 20.8 points, 1.4 steals and 2.1 three-pointers per game over 50 regular-season appearances. The door is now open for Vit Krejci and Jeremy Sochan to compete for bench minutes during camp.

injury.shortComment: Harris (calf) is listed as out for Saturday's game against Minnesota.
injury.detail: Harris suffered a strained left calf ahead of the 2026-27 campaign and has yet to make his debut with the Spurs. The veteran is slowly making progress toward a return, though he should be considered week-to-week until more information is released. The 34-year-old, who signed with San Antonio during the offseason, averaged 13.3 points, 5.1 rebounds and 2.5 assists over 27.7 minutes per contest in 63 regular-season appearances with the Pistons in 2025-26.

injury.shortComment: Quaintance has been around the team but has not yet been cleared for basketball activities, Matt Guzman of SI.com reports.
injury.detail: The Spurs are expected to exercise extreme caution with the big man, as Quaintance suffered a torn ACL and meniscus with Arizona State in February 2025 before appearing in only four games with Kentucky last season due to severe complications and persistent swelling. The 19-year-old underwent a cleanup procedure on his meniscus in mid-July, and the Spurs will likely want him at 100 percent before ramping him up to basketball activities.
